briefFidelity: FAIL, and the failure is at the centre of the brief rather than at its edges. THICKET asks for profusion rather than arrangement, and for no rest anywhere in the composition. Before I had read a word of it I described these frames as a rosette, a mandala, a rose window, a medallion inscribed in a square with its corners cut to black -- arrangement in its purest form, six-fold rotational symmetry registered dead centre in every one of the twelve. And the single largest element of 1203347, 1475115, 1733538 and 1243682 is a flat, empty, perfectly centred khaki disc occupying roughly a third of the frame: that is not a thicket with a clearing in it, it is a place of rest sitting exactly where the eye is sent. The brief also asks that the density read as mass rather than as pattern; strict kaleidoscopic symmetry makes 1283437, 1310661, 1835793 and 1991107 read as pattern first and mass second. Two seeds fail the density clause outright in the other direction: 1446330 and 1561509 are black-dominant fields of scattered orange confetti, sparse rather than near-saturated, and 1366079 is a nearly empty pale frame with one black pinprick at its centre. What IS delivered is the colour sentence -- rust, copper and umber over near-black, values close together -- and roughly three quarters of the state sentence. That is not enough to make the picture the thing that was commissioned.
composition: Every frame has a focal hierarchy and it is the same hierarchy twelve times: a differentiated core inside an annulus of hexagons that bleeds off all four edges. Something does dominate -- the core -- and it is clearly deliberate, but it is the wrong dominance for a brief that wants incident everywhere. The surround is an even, unhierarchical carpet: in 1203347, 1475115 and 1733538 no individual hexagon or cluster in the outer field earns any attention. The frame is not really used; the medallion floats at the exact centre of the square and the corners are surrendered to black in 1203347, 1243682, 1985692 and 1991107, so the work is a centred object in a square rather than a field that occupies one. 1446330 is the only token that pushes incident right out to the edges and it does so by inverting the whole scheme.
collectionCoherence: This reads unmistakably as ONE project, and if anything the coherence is the problem rather than a virtue. All twelve share the palette, the translucent convex-polygon vocabulary, the six-fold centred symmetry, the soft edges and the black-cornered medallion silhouette: 1203347, 1243682, 1283437, 1310661, 1475115, 1733538, 1835793, 1985692 and 1991107 are visibly siblings on the contact sheet. Only 1446330 and 1561509 break the family, and they break it by inverting figure and ground rather than by leaving it -- they still use the same hexagons and the same orange. This is not a folder of unrelated tokens; it is a collection with a single strong idea repeated.
palette: The hue family looks genuinely chosen and matches the brief: terracotta, rust, copper and umber over a near-black ground, held in a narrow band so overlapping translucent hexagons separate by only a small value step. That closeness is deliberate and it works in 1733538 and 1985692, where the stacking builds mass. Two problems. First, the desaturated olive-grey carrying the cores of 1203347, 1243682, 1475115 and 1733538 is off-family -- it is neither rust nor copper nor umber, it reads as fog rather than as a colour, and it occupies the largest single area in those tokens. Second, the contrast range does very little work inside the field: in 1203347 and 1475115 the orange tints are so close that the polygon overlaps barely register and the surround goes flat. The black ground supports the drawing where it appears and never competes.
seedVariation: Both failure directions are present at once. In the middle, 1203347, 1475115 and 1733538 are close to the same work at three rotations -- orange field, khaki blob, black corner wedges -- and 1243682 is a fourth near-neighbour with a smaller core; the differences are of scale and density, not of structure. At the ends, 1446330 and 1561509 invert figure and ground so completely that they look like output from a different generator, and 1366079 -- an almost unbroken pale field with a single black point dead centre -- reads as a failure state rather than as a member. So the project is simultaneously too narrow where most of its mass sits and too wide at its two extremes. The brief asked tokens to differ in density AND structure; they differ in density and share one structure.
thumbnailSurvival: At 120px the twelve collapse into about four families rather than twelve things: orange field with khaki blob (1203347, 1475115, 1733538, and 1243682 at a squint), orange field with speckled core (1283437, 1310661, 1835793, 1985692, 1991107), black confetti field (1446330, 1561509), and near-empty pale field (1366079). Within the first family I cannot tell 1203347 from 1475115 from 1733538. Everything inside the cores -- the dot spirals of 1283437, 1310661, 1991107 -- goes to a single grey smudge. What survives is the shared silhouette and the black corners, which is exactly the part that does not individuate a token. And the brief's promise, an intricate field that rewards a long look and finds structure at every scale, is precisely what does not survive: at browse size there is one scale.
marketResponse: Partly delivered, and honestly so in three of the four seeds shown. 1243682 is the strongest: stress replaces the neutral dark octagon with a hard black star-shaped halo that is unmistakable at 120px, and recovery fills it with a mottled khaki plate. 1310661 is next -- neutral is a loose scatter of dots, stress collapses to a black hexagonal void with a small ring inside, recovery re-blooms into a dotted lattice -- and it is obvious at browse size. 1283437 tightens its spiral and adds concentric dark banding under stress, then spreads wider and larger in recovery; visible, if less loud. 1203347 fails the brief's explicit test: its three states at 120px are the same picture, a khaki blob in an orange field, separated only by a slight change in the blob edge. The direction is also wrong. The brief asks the THICKET to thin and open; what actually thins is a hole at the centre, while the outer hexagon field of 1203347 and 1283437 is essentially unchanged between neutral and stress.
tokenIdentity: Holds well, and in one case too well. Across the three states 1243682 keeps its ring-around-a-core plan, 1283437 keeps its dot spiral, 1310661 keeps its lattice-and-scatter, and 1203347 keeps its blob-in-field; none of the four is replaced by a different object under drawdown, and the palette and symmetry never move. 1310661 travels furthest -- the stress black void is a large change -- but the recovery frame plainly returns to the neutral token rather than to a new one. The one caution is 1203347, where identity is preserved so completely that it comes at the cost of the state response above.
artifacts: Edges are soft throughout: at 512px the large polygons look rendered slightly out of focus, which reads as haze at 256 and as blur at 120. The black corner wedges in 1203347, 1243682 and 1985692 have hard straight cuts that read as shapes clipped against a boundary rather than as chosen edges. In 1366079 a single tiny black dot sits exactly at centre and reads as a stray pinprick, not a mark. 1446330 and 1561509 have hexagons cut in half by the viewBox at all four edges; that is defensible as tiling, but beside the inscribed medallion of the other ten it reads as clipping. The low-value khaki cores of 1203347 and 1475115 fog rather than draw, and in 1310661 neutral the dot ring nearly vanishes into the field. No collisions into mush and no outright breakage.
reasoning: The gate decided this. Working blind, with no knowledge that a brief existed, I described these frames as a mandala, a rose window, a medallion floating dead centre in a square with its corners cut to black -- and I named the large flat empty disc at the middle of 1203347, 1475115, 1733538 and 1243682 as the subject of the picture. The brief then asked for the opposite of both of those things: profusion rather than arrangement, and no rest anywhere in the composition. Strict six-fold symmetry registered at the centre of every token is arrangement, and a flat empty core occupying a third of the frame is rest, placed exactly where the eye lands. That is not a near miss of tone; it is the work reading as a different kind of object than the one commissioned. The supporting axes do not rescue it: two seeds (1446330, 1561509) are sparse where near-saturation was asked for, one (1366079) is nearly blank, three (1203347, 1475115, 1733538) are interchangeable at browse size, and 1203347's three market states are indistinguishable at 120px against a brief that made that difference an explicit requirement. The colour is right and three of four seeds do move visibly under stress, so this is competent work -- but competent at being a kaleidoscopic rose window, not a thicket.
wouldChange: Break the registration first: the six-fold rotational symmetry centred on the frame is what converts profusion into arrangement, so either drop it entirely or offset and perturb it per seed so no token is a mirror of itself. Second, fill the core -- the khaki discs of 1203347, 1475115, 1733538 and 1243682 should carry the densest, finest incident in the frame rather than the least, and the off-family olive should be replaced by an umber inside the stated rust/copper range. Third, introduce at least two more scales of element: the current hexagons occupy one or two sizes, which is why nothing survives a long look at 256 and why the 120px sheet flattens to four families; small-scale incident laid over the large plates would give the eye somewhere to go. Fourth, make stress thin the WHOLE field rather than grow a hole at the centre -- 1203347's outer annulus should visibly open, since that is the change the brief actually asked for and the one seed where the state response is currently invisible at browse size. Finally, pull 1446330, 1561509 and 1366079 back toward the density band or accept that the density parameter reaches sparseness the brief excludes.
